text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing the decreased vision and black spots in your right eye? Also, are you currently on any antiretroviral therapy, and do you have any eye pain or redness?

text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and recent fungal esophagitis, have you missed any doses of your antiretroviral therapy recently? Also, do the black spots appear to be moving with your eye movements, like floating cobwebs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the clarification; have you noticed any flashes of light or a shadow curtain appearing in your peripheral vision? Also, could you confirm if the black spots seem to be stationary or if they float when you move your eye?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy reveals granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4 Count shows 36/mm3.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities with hemorrhages, combined with your critically low CD4 count, strongly suggest Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Given these specific signs and your AIDS history, I can now confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis
